    Where you live changes your footprint

    dorm life

    • Use a switched power strip for your desk and turn it off when you leave. Chargers and monitors keep drawing power on standby.
    • Share one mini-fridge with your roommate. A fridge runs 24/7, roughly 30 kWh a month.
    • Wash full loads in cold water and skip the dryer when you can. Most laundry energy goes to heat.
    • Unplug the fridge and electronics before breaks, and ask your RA about move-out checklists.
    • Set laptops and monitors to sleep after 5 minutes, and keep windows shut while the heat or AC runs.
    • Start a floor challenge. Many campuses run dorm-vs-dorm energy contests. Ask your RA or sustainability office.

    about

    hi, i'm charles.

    I'm an energy engineering student at UC Berkeley. I'm interested in sustainable energy, the power grid, and how sustainability shows up in everyday life: the lamp on your desk, the laundry you run, the outlet you plug into.

    I built Gridlocal because the numbers on a power bill don't tell you where your electricity comes from or what you can do about it. It starts with college students, since dorms, first apartments and first leases are where energy habits form. The grid figures are regional estimates today, and live data is next.
